damageAllocation.description: When weapons fire penetrates a downed shield, damage is distributed throughout the ship's internal systems. This subsystem damage is the core of SFB's damage model — only when most systems are destroyed does damage go to the hull's excess damage track.

step1.name: Shield Absorption
step1.description: Incoming damage is first applied to the shield facing the attacker. Reinforcement points absorb damage before shield boxes.

step2.name: Shield Down Check
step2.description: If the shield has no remaining boxes, it is 'down.' Remaining damage proceeds to internal systems.

step3.name: Damage Allocation Roll
step3.description: For each point of damage that penetrates, roll on the Damage Allocation Chart. The result determines which internal system is hit.

step4.name: System Damage
step4.description: Mark out the indicated box on the SSD. Destroyed systems cannot be used. If a system has no remaining boxes, the damage may be redirected or go to excess damage.

step5.name: Excess Damage
step5.description: When most systems are destroyed, remaining damage is allocated to the excess damage track. When excess damage fills up, the ship is destroyed.

damageAllocationChart.description: Each ship has its own Damage Allocation Chart on its SSD. The chart maps die rolls to specific systems that can be damaged.

systemCategories.description: Left and right warp engines. Damage reduces available energy output.
systemCategories.effect: Reduced energy production, potentially cascading into lower speed and weapon power.

systemCategories.description: Left and right impulse engines. Damage reduces impulse power and sublight capability.
systemCategories.effect: Reduced impulse energy and movement capability.

systemCategories.description: Systems that generate shield power. Damage may reduce shield capacity.
Individual weapon banks. Damage destroys weapons.
systemCategories.effect: Lost weapon capability. Specific phasers, disruptors, or torpedo launchers become inoperable.

systemCategories.description: Main bridge and control spaces. Damage impairs ship command.
systemCategories.effect: Lost control spaces affect fleet command capability and may cripple the ship.

systemCategories.description: Damage control track. Damage reduces repair capability.
systemCategories.effect: Lower DamCon rating means fewer shield repairs per turn.

systemCategories.description: Cloaking devices, tractor beams, transporters, labs, batteries, capacitors.
Structural integrity. Excess damage goes here.
systemCategories.effect: When excess damage track is full, the ship is destroyed.

excessDamage.description: The excess damage track represents the ship's remaining structural integrity after systems are destroyed.
excessDamage.calculation: Excess damage capacity = Hull boxes ÷ 4 (approximately). Varies by ship.
excessDamage.destruction: When the excess damage track is filled, the ship is destroyed and may explode.

damageControl.description: Damage Control (DamCon) is the ability to repair shields during a scenario without external facilities.
damageControl.rating: The highest undestroyed box on the DamCon track determines the current rating.
damageControl.repairRate: DamCon rating = number of shield points that can be repaired per turn.
limitations: Can only repair shields, not internal systems (during tactical play)
DamCon parties also seal hull ruptures and prevent fires — this is factored into the rules and can be ignored by players
If DamCon is fully destroyed, no shield repair is possible

campaignRepairs.description: In campaign play, ships with repair systems can perform strategic repairs between battles.
campaignRepairs.rate: Each Repair box produces 1 repair point every strategic impulse.
campaignRepairs.limitation: If the ship is not fully repaired, it must dock with a repair unit for further campaign repairs.

crippledCondition.description: A ship is crippled when it loses all control spaces or both warp engines.
effects: Crew may be evacuated by friendly ships

selfDestruction.description: A crippled or voluntarily sacrificing ship can self-destruct, creating a large explosion.
effects: Damages nearby ships within a radius

tacticalNotes: Destroying enemy warp engines is a priority — it reduces their energy for everything.
DamCon destruction prevents shield repair, making the ship increasingly vulnerable.
Weapon destruction reduces the enemy's offensive capability.
Control space destruction can cripple a ship before it is fully destroyed.
The Damage Allocation system means ships can absorb significant damage before being destroyed.
